text: {"distance_m": 1.4, "reasoning_short": "Estimate only: there is no single exact cutoff. Small low-contrast spots obey Ricco's law, where threshold contrast × spot area is roughly constant. Assume a ~100% contrast dot is just detectable at ~1 arcmin under indoor light. Then a 15% contrast spot needs about 6–7× the area, or ~2.5 arcmin across (~7.3e-4 rad). A 1 mm spot subtends that angle at 1 mm / 7.3e-4 ≈ 1.4 m."}
